question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5{x}^{2}+22x}}$ at the point where $x=2$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=5{x}^{2}+22x.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10x+22.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (10x+22) \\  & =-\frac{10x+22}{2\sqrt{(5{x}^{2}+22x{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & ={(-\frac{10x+22}{2\sqrt{(5{x}^{2}+22x{)}^{3}}})|}_{x=2} \\  & =-\frac{10(2)+22}{2\sqrt{(5(2{)}^{2}+22(2){)}^{3}}} \\  & =-\frac{42}{2\sqrt{{64}^{3}}} \\  & =-\frac{21}{512}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
